description_full: Light S.A., together with its subsidiaries, engages in the generation, transmission, distribution, and sale of electric power in Brazil. The company distributes electricity in the state of Rio de Janeiro. It engages in the research, planning, building, operation, and exploration of generation and transmission systems; purchase, sale, import, and export of electricity, thermal power, and gas and industrial utilities; provision of consulting services in the energy sector; lease of real estate and personal properties; acquisition and sale of goods related to the studies and projects; implementation, operation, and maintenance of construction works and facilities; analysis of technical and economic feasibility; and hydropower generation activities. In addition, the company provides services to low voltage clients, including the assembly, renovation, and maintenance of facilities. Further, it offers technology solutions and systems for the operating management of public service concessionaires, including electricity, gas, water, sewage and other utility companies; and builds, installs, operates, and explores electric power plants. The company primarily serves residential, commercial, industrial, commercial, rural, government, advertising, and utility customers. The company was founded in 1899 and is headquartered in Rio De Janeiro, Brazil.

financial_summary: Light S.A. is a small-cap utilities business with a $765M market cap on $2.5B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +1% over the past three years, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.

Returns on capital run at 7% against a 5% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically, and 13% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The company is burning through $183M of cash, and without positive owner earnings any valuation rests on hope rather than evidence.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 3.7× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 2.5× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
